subject: Decommission & field suppression workflow for regulated tenants

We need to wind down one of our sandbox tenants that contains recent claims data and associated PII/PHI. Before we move forward, Compliance asked for a clear write-up of options and the operational runbook for:

- Permanent deletion vs irreversible suppression/pseudonymization of identifiers

Hi Monica — thanks for the note and the attachment. High level answers up front, then proposed items/actions: 

1) Options (tradeoffs)
- Immediate irrevocable delete: remove object stores, drop DB rows, scrub KV caches. Strongest auditor answer but takes coordination for snapshots/backups. Recommended when retention floor = 0.
- Irreversible suppression (recommended for many regulated scenarios): replace direct identifiers with non-reversible hashes (salted + site-wide pepper) and remove direct contact fields. Keeps analytic aggregates but prevents re-identification without out-of-band keys.
- Pseudonymization reversible by customer (token service): we can return tokens that you control; Redwood-held reversible tokens are not recommended for regulated PHI unless contractually required.

2) Retention floors
- Audit logs and request traces: we can retain for configurable windows. Default hosted policy is 365 days; Dedicated allows shorter (90 days) if agreed in contract.
- Raw message/record retention: configurable per-tenant. We support retention cutoffs (delete records older than X) and eviction jobs.

3) Deletion evidence
- We produce deletion manifests (object UUIDs, timestamps) and SHA256 manifests for S3 objects prior to removal. For DB row deletes we provide SQL run outputs and job IDs.

Proposed runbook (draft)
- Day 0: Legal hold check (customer to confirm outstanding holds).
- Day 1–3: Freeze writes, snapshot S3 + DB (for forensics), export held artifacts to encrypted archive (retained per hold).
- Day 4–14: Run suppression job (replace identifiers per map), run QA sampling, run audit log export.
- Day 15–45: Purge legacy artifacts and run final deletion jobs; deliver deletion manifest and proof-of-deletion.

Questions for you:
- What is MedicaSure's minimum retention for claims and for contact-level PII? (You mentioned recent claims — what window?)
- Do you need reversible tokens for any downstream systems?

If it helps I can loop in Neha (data platform) and Priyom (solutions) for specifics — copying them here. Happy to set a call.

—Jordan Blake
Director, Account Solutions | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Tenant decommission: regulated dataset questions

Adding technical detail from infra/ops side. Short answers and constraints: 

- Redaction approach: for PHI we prefer deterministic irreversible tokenization at deletion time. Implementation: replace direct identifiers (name, SSN, email, phone) with salted SHA256 hashes; drop free-text notes that contain PHI unless customer authorizes field-level extraction. See attached redaction_spec.xlsx (stub).

- KV cache and model caches: we purge KV caches and ephemeral caches on job runtime; persistent caches (if configured by customer) require an explicit purge window — those are included in the deletion manifest.

- Backups & snapshots: by default we snapshot S3 and DB before destructive ops and hold those snapshots for 30 days unless a longer legal hold is requested. If MedicaSure requires a shorter window we can accelerate destruction but must be explicit in contract.

- Proof-of-deletion: we publish a signed manifest (job id, object list, sha256, timestamp) and a deletion runbook entry. For DB deletes we provide the row ids and a job trace; for object stores we provide object keys + digest.

- SLA expectations: for Dedicated customers we typically offer a 30–45 day end-to-end window from freeze -> final delete. Hosted customers follow a 45–90 day window due to multi-tenant snapshot schedules.

I'll attach a field suppression map that lists exact columns we plan to transform. Also note: reversible tokens are only issued if you host the token service or we place tokenization keys in your KMS. Redwood will not hold reversible keys for PHI unless explicitly contracted under stronger controls.

-Neha Kapoor
Sr. Engineering Manager, Data Platform | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Tenant decommission: regulated dataset questions

Thanks Jordan and Neha — helpful. Some clarifications from Compliance: 

- MedicaSure policy: claims records must be retained for 180 days for analytics (aggregate), but direct-contact PII must be suppressed within 30 days of decommission start. We need a proof package for both the suppression step and the final deletion of supporting raw artifacts.

- Reversibility: we cannot accept reversible tokens retained by a vendor. If you provide hashes, please confirm your process uses a salt+pepper model where only MedicaSure holds the pepper (or provide a customer-managed KMS). Otherwise we will consider those hashes reversible and not compliant.

- Legal hold: possibility of two small litigation holds (one active case) — if a legal hold is asserted we will notify you within Day 0 and expect immediate freeze.

Can you provide a conservative timeline that meets these constraints and the exact deliverables we will receive (manifests, signed receipts, deletion job IDs)? Also can you confirm whether ephemeral memcache entries are part of your deletion manifest?

I can escalate if needed but would prefer to align on a runbook and sign-off.

-Monica
Head of Compliance — MedicaSure

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@medicasure.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant decommission: regulated dataset questions

Monica — thanks for the specifics. Below is a conservative, auditable runbook tailored to MedicaSure (attach: decommission_flow.pdf and field_suppression_map.csv). Forwarding the plan to legal and ops for sign-off.

Summary timeline (conservative)
- Day 0 (Agreement): Customer signs runbook + confirms holds. Freeze writes immediately.
- Day 1: Snapshot DB + S3 -> encrypted archive (forensics). Generate snapshot manifest (sha256).
- Day 2–5: Suppression pass: replace contact fields with salted SHA256 (salt managed by Redwood; pepper to be provided by MedicaSure KMS if you want non-reversible; if no pepper provided we will use a customer-rotatable key and document key custody). See field_suppression_map.csv (attached).
- Day 6–14: QA sampling & audit: 1% + targeted records. Provide redaction report and sampling hashes.
- Day 15–45: Final purge of snapshots and raw artifacts (unless legal hold). Deliver final deletion manifest and signed proof-of-deletion (job id + object list + sha256 digests).

Proof artifacts we will deliver
- Snapshot manifest (sha256 + timestamp)
- Suppression run log (job id, mapping of columns transformed, number of rows touched)
- QA sampling report (hashes of samples + sample selection seed)
- Final deletion manifest (object keys + digest + deletion run id)
- Signed PDF runbook entry with ops signature

Ephemeral caches: yes, we include memcache/KV eviction entries in the deletion manifest when those caches are tenant-scoped. Host-wide ephemeral caches that include aggregated shared content are cleared to tenant-scope where possible; if full eviction isn’t feasible we will document residual keys and proof of attempted purge.

Reversibility: we will not retain pepper keys. Option A: MedicaSure supplies pepper in your KMS (recommended) so Redwood never has reversible tokens. Option B: Redwood holds key under HSM with strict access controls and audit (requires contractual change).

Next steps / action items
- Monica: confirm acceptance of timeline and whether MedicaSure will provide a pepper via KMS (yes/no).
- MedicaSure legal: confirm any active holds and provide hold IDs.
- Redwood ops (Neha/Priyom): prepare suppression script and a QA schedule; I will open the deletion run ticket once we have sign-off.

If that all looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute call to walk the runbook and sign-off checklist.

Thanks — Jordan
Director, Account Solutions | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
